output.normalized_title: search-indexer: Expired OAuth certificate on identity-provider (search-indexer)

output.classification_reasoning: The failure originates from an expired OAuth certificate on the identity-provider, which is an authentication mechanism. The search-indexer depends on valid tokens from the identity-provider, so the expired certificate prevents token issuance, leading to service degradation and a telemetry spike. Resolving the issue requires certificate renewal, coordination with the identity-provider, and verification of token flows across services, which involves more than a simple configuration tweak but does not require deep architectural changes, placing the incident at a moderate level of operational complexity.

prerequisites: Root access or AWS SSO role ProdOperations
output.security_notes: Do not terminate primary node without promoting read-replica first. Verify write freeze before reboot.

diagnostic_stage_assessment.notes: Current incident mirrors historical authentication failure (INC-1007) with the same expired OAuth certificate symptom, indicating a recurring auth issue in search-indexer.

output.governing_sla_rule: Tier-1 service impacting >= 500 users, or cross-tier impact >= 2,000 users.
output.justification: The incident affects 15,000 users, far exceeding the cross‑tier impact threshold of 2,000 users defined in the SLA rule. Although the service tier is Tier‑3, the rule applies across tiers when the user impact surpasses 2,000, triggering SEV‑2. The outage duration of 10 minutes is within the acceptable window for SEV‑2 classification, and the root‑cause confirmation (expired OAuth certificate) aligns with a known recurring authentication issue, reinforcing the severity assessment.

remediation_steps.title: Validate Operator Access and Cluster Context
remediation_steps.description: Ensure the engineer has the required ProdOperations role and that kubectl is pointed at the production cluster in us-east-1.
verification: AWS identity matches ProdOperations role
kubectl context output contains prod-us-east-1
Master node list is reachable

remediation_steps.title: Inspect Current OAuth Certificate on Identity Provider
remediation_steps.description: Query the secret storing the OAuth certificate to confirm expiration date and capture the current fingerprint for rollback.
commands: kubectl -n identity get secret oauth-cert -o jsonpath='{.data.tls\.crt}' | base64 --decode | openssl x509 -noout -dates
kubectl -n identity get secret oauth-cert -o jsonpath='{.data.tls\.crt}' | base64 --decode | openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint
verification: Expiration date is in the past (e.g., "notAfter=Jan  1 00:00:00 2024 GMT")
Fingerprint recorded for later comparison

remediation_steps.title: Rotate OAuth Certificate
remediation_steps.description: Create a new certificate, update the Kubernetes secret, and trigger a rolling restart of the identity‑provider deployment so the new cert is loaded.
commands: # Generate new cert (example using existing internal CA)
kubectl -n identity create secret generic oauth-cert --from-file=tls.crt=/tmp/oauth.crt --from-file=tls.key=/tmp/oauth.key --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
verification: kubectl -n identity get secret oauth-cert -o jsonpath='{.data.tls\.crt}' | base64 --decode | openssl x509 -noout -dates' shows future notAfter date
Pods in deployment/identity-provider report READY=desired/desired and no CrashLoopBackOff
Identity provider logs contain "certificate successfully reloaded"

remediation_steps.title: Refresh Dependent Service (search-indexer)
remediation_steps.description: Force a rolling restart of the search-indexer deployment so it picks up the refreshed OAuth token validation path.
verification: All search-indexer pods reach READY=1/1 without restart errors
curl -sSf https://search-indexer.internal/healthz returns HTTP 200 with "status":"OK"

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit
remediation_steps.description: Validate that authentication errors have ceased and that end‑user traffic is restored.
commands: kubectl logs -n search -l app=search-indexer --since=5m | grep ERR_AUTHENTICATION_ISSUE_818 || echo 'No auth errors'
verification: Gateway health endpoint returns OK
Log grep returns no matching authentication error lines
AuthErrorRate metric sum is 0 for the last 10 minutes

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: Revert the OAuth certificate secret to the previous version and undo any rolling restarts, then verify service health before declaring rollback complete.

steps.title: Restore Previous OAuth Certificate Secret
steps.description: Replace the current oauth‑cert secret with the captured fingerprint from step 2.
commands: # Assuming the previous cert was saved as /tmp/old_oauth.crt and key as /tmp/old_oauth.key
kubectl -n identity create secret generic oauth-cert --from-file=tls.crt=/tmp/old_oauth.crt --from-file=tls.key=/tmp/old_oauth.key --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
verification: Secret data matches the original fingerprint recorded in step 2
Identity provider pods restart cleanly and logs show "using existing certificate"

steps.title: Undo Search‑Indexer Rolling Restart (if needed)
steps.description: If the new certificate caused regressions, rollback the search-indexer deployment to the prior replica set.
verification: Deployment reports revision reverted to the pre‑remediation version
Pods reach READY=1/1 and logs show no auth‑related errors

steps.title: Confirm System Health After Rollback
steps.description: Run the same health audit as in the remediation to ensure the environment is stable.
commands: kubectl logs -n search -l app=search-indexer --since=5m | grep ERR_AUTHENTICATION_ISSUE_818 || echo 'No auth errors'
verification: Gateway health endpoint returns OK
No authentication error logs appear
AuthErrorRate metric remains at 0

prerequisite_checks: Operator credentials verified for ProdOperations role
Current kubectl context points to prod-us-east-1
Backup of existing oauth‑cert secret exported to /tmp/old_oauth.*
Rollback procedure documented and approved by change management
